title: DDIA 12 · STREAM PROCESSING
subtitle: Batch on an unbounded input: process each event as it arrives, keep derived systems in sync, and handle late and duplicate events.
footer: Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.

head: Queue (RabbitMQ, SQS, JMS)
Log (Kafka, Kinesis, Pulsar)
rows: Message stays; consumer just advances an offset
Any consumer takes any message (load balancing)
One consumer per partition per group
Yes: reset offset, re-read days of history
Task queues: send email, resize image, each job independent
Event streams: ordering matters, multiple consumers, replay, CDC

blocks.text: "Image resize jobs go on SQS, since they are independent with per-message retry.
Another group reads the same data independently with its own offsets. Adding consumers doesn't cost the producer anything.
And if the app crashes between the two writes, one system has the change and the other doesn't. Writing to two systems is never atomic.
Every derived system (search, cache, warehouse) consumes the log and updates itself. Each can be rebuilt by replaying from offset 0, or from a snapshot plus the log.
State is a derived view, a fold over the events. You can build new views later by replaying, and debug by replaying to any point in time.
Apply each change's delta to the stored result (Materialize, RisingWave, Feldera). Reads are instant and fresh.
Session: group a user's activity until a gap, as in web analytics and Strava activities.
Replay means some outputs are sent twice.

items: Kafka partitioned by ad_id → Flink 1-min tumbling windows on event time → OLAP store. Raw clicks to S3 for batch reconciliation.
"Keep search, cache, and DB in sync?"
CDC (Debezium) or outbox → Kafka → idempotent consumers. Never dual-write.
Ordering, replay, or many consumers → Kafka. Independent tasks with per-message retry and DLQ → SQS.
"At-least-once delivery plus idempotent processing equals effectively-once. I make the consumer idempotent with an event ID."
